title: The Alternative Model of Personality Disorders: Associations with Childhood Experiences, Attachment Patterns, Interpersonal Problems, and Current Psychopathology
summary:
Background: Personality disorders have traditionally been described using fixed diagnostic categories. More recent approaches, however, focus on a dimensional understanding of mental health, placing emphasis on how well a person functions in everyday life rather than on specific symptom lists. This so-called Alternative Model for Personality Disorders has been adapted for the international diagnostic classification system ICD-11 and is expected to be used in routine clinical practice.
Research Question: The aim of this study is to examine this new diagnostic model in patients receiving clinical treatment. The study will assess personality functioning (SCID-5-AMPD) and explore how it is related to important life and health factors, such as adverse childhood experiences, interpersonal relationships, attachment patterns, the ability to understand one’s own and others’ thoughts and feelings, and current psychological symptoms.
Methods: The study is conducted as a one-time cross-sectional assessment. Participants will take part in clinical interviews and complete standardized questionnaires. The results are intended to improve understanding of whether this new diagnostic approach is useful for clinical practice and whether it allows for a more accurate and meaningful assessment of mental health problems. In the long term, the findings may contribute to improving diagnosis and treatment in routine mental health care.

interventions.name: Participation in structured clinical interviews (SCID-5-AMPD) and completion of standardized questionnaires assessing personality functioning and key influencing factors, including traumatic childhood experiences, attachment style, interpersonal problems, mentalizing capacity, and current psychopath

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Sufficient proficiency in German, both spoken and written, to reliably complete questionnaires and participate in interviews.
Adequate concentration ability and psychological stability to participate in an interview and complete questionnaire assessments.
Exclusion criteria:
Pregnancy
Acute psychotic symptoms
Severe cognitive impairment
Significant emotional destabilization that precludes reliable participation in the assessments
